area.reviews.1.quote: Sorry version: Super helpful, straight forward and made sure we had heat ASAP. TLDR; VERSION: My heater went out at 5am. I called after 7am, technician showed at 8:30 to verify the issue and what part was needed. Then went to his scheduled 9am that was close by. He ordered the part, picked it up and had the heater fully repaired before 1.
area.reviews.2.quote: Our A/C stopped working during the recent heat wave. Other companies didn't return our messages, but City & Suburban answered right away and were professional and communicative throughout. Rob was able to get to our place within a few hours, and he quickly diagnosed and fixed our A/C unit. He was practical and professional, and we would definitely call again.
area.reviews.3.quote: Super responsive, knowledgeable and friendly with very fair prices and quality work. Have used them the last 2 years to recharge my AC refrigerant and never got up sold. AC went out again this week, called for an appointment on Tuesday and was able to get one same day. Needed a new AC unit this time, and could have gotten it installed as early as the next day.
area.reviews.4.quote: Rob and the team at City Suburban are top notch. I’ve been using them for several years now for annual checkups of my system and have nothing but good things to say. He is respectful of my space, my questions, and has always been punctual. No upsells, just what I need for reliable AC and heat throughout the year. They’ve always been accommodating meeting my scheduling needs, as well.
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a ranch, an older house and a shop
area.scope.1.why: East of Ridge, older houses often run boilers; west of Ridge, 1950s ranches and bi-levels run furnaces.
area.scope.2.why: Radiator-heated houses east of Ridge have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.3.why: Larger Wilmette houses can run a furnace and AC for each floor, so a repair starts with finding which one has failed.
area.scope.4.why: Ranches and bi-levels often keep the furnace in a utility room; older houses keep theirs in the basement.
area.scope.5.why: Shops on Central Ave and at Plaza del Lago run rooftop units, so roof access and opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.faq.heading: Wilmette HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the furnace in my Wilmette ranch worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Wilmette from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Can you work on the boiler in an older house east of Ridge?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Wilmette need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the furnace has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace, boiler or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. East of Ridge, tell us if the house heats with radiators.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Wilmette is on our service area list, about 11 miles north of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Boiler service is on our list: pressure, circulators, zone valves and venting, in older houses and vintage two-flats.
extras.faq.4.a: It depends on the job. The Village of Wilmette sets its own permit rules, mostly for installs and replacements. A repair or tune-up is a different job. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.
